title: More GPT marking data - is it better than humans at predicting future grades?
author: Chris Wheadon and Daisy Christodoulou
source: Chris Wheadon and Daisy Christodoulou (substack.nomoremarking.com), March 25, 2023
summary: In a follow-up to their first GPT-3 marking trial, No More Marking tests whether GPT-3 or human judges better predict pupils' Year 6 writing scores from Year 5 essays. They transcribed 156 handwritten Year 5 essays and compared human Comparative Judgement and GPT marks against the same pupils' later writing. Human judging correlated at 0.73 with the Year 6 scores, while GPT marking managed only 0.54. The authors again saw GPT marks on the same grade spanning nearly the whole human quality scale. They frame themselves as reluctant sceptics who invested heavily in the technology and are simply following the data.
points: Human judging of Year 5 essays predicted Year 6 writing scores at 0.73 over 18 months, versus 0.54 for GPT-3, so the AI has weaker predictive validity.
The study design is systematic and larger-scale, with 156 transcribed essays, as an explicit answer to viral one-off examples of ChatGPT giving a perfect mark.
Essays given the same GPT mark spanned almost the entire human-judged quality range, repeating the clustering problem from the first trial.
The authors' scepticism is data-led, since they built the tooling expecting AI marking to be enormously useful.
quotes: We are not natural AI sceptics - we wouldn't have gone to this bother if we were! We have used different AI models very successfully on another website we run, Automark, and could see that if GPT could mark essays it would be enormously useful.

These generally tend to be one-off examples, and ChatGPT certainly does give some essays the right mark, just as a stopped clock is right twice a day. We are trying to do something more systematic at a larger scale, which is why we did the technical work to plug GPT into our software.
From our archive of writing, we transcribed 156 year 5 essays on the subject ‘My ideal job’. All the essays were handwritten and undertaken in exam conditions.
The human judging in year 5 shows a correlation of 0.73 to the year 6 writing scores, which is high given the assessments were taken 18 months apart.
The GPT marking in year 5 shows a correlation of 0.54 to the year 6 writing scores, which is substantially lower than the human to human correlation.
Once again we see the same issues with the GPT marking. Essays on the same GPT mark span almost the entire range of the human judging quality scale.
